newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria, Russia, Greece mull oil pipeline funding.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, Russia, Greece mull oil pipeline funding.

text.p: Bulgaria, Russia and Greece have discussed financing of a planned oil route supplying Russian crude to the Balkans at a two-day experts' meeting, a Bulgarian official said on Monday.

Tsveta Kamenova of the Construction Ministry said Bulgaria and Russia would seek creditors for the pipeline, expected to cost some $600-$700 million, while Greece could rely mainly on the European Union's structural funds.
The three countries have worked out feasibility studies, expected to cost $10 million.

"At our meeting last week (Thursday and Friday) in Sofia we decided to set up a working group, which will unite the feasibility studies into one and that is why some more work in this direction is still needed," Kamenova told Reuters.

Russia, Bulgaria and Greece plan a tanker route from the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk to Bourgas in Bulgaria from where a new pipeline would carry Russian crude to Alexandroupolis in Greece.
A tripartite meeting at government level was delayed due to elections in Russia and Greece. Bulgaria has presidential elections on October 27.
Bulgarian deputy prime minister Doncho Konakchiev said recently the route was now being considered as a part of a greater regional project linking the Black Sea to a Caspian Sea oil pipeline.
